planting.note: Plant rhizomes in heavy, fertile aquatic soil in submerged containers 12-24 inches deep in a full-sun pond after last frost; Attraction water lily is a vigorous, cold-hardy variety that overwinters in the pond in most temperate climates.

directions: Plant rhizomes in heavy, fertile aquatic soil in submerged containers 12-24 inches deep in a full-sun pond after last frost; Attraction water lily is a vigorous, cold-hardy variety that overwinters in the pond in most temperate climates. One of the classic old Marliac-bred hardy water lilies, it produces large, star-shaped flowers in a rich garnet-red that deepens further with age, flecked with white at the petal bases, opening in succession from late spring through fall above broad, purple-tinged green pads. Its vigorous, spreading growth makes it well suited to a larger pond where it has room to fill in, providing both dramatic bloom color and valuable shade coverage over the water's surface to help control algae. Feed with aquatic plant tablets monthly through the growing season, remove spent flowers and yellowing pads, and divide overcrowded rhizomes every three to four years.
sources: International Waterlily and Water Gardening Society

planting.note: Plant rhizome divisions in spring in wet, fertile soil in shallow standing water up to 4 inches deep or consistently saturated soil in full sun to partial shade; variegated Japanese water iris needs constant moisture and struggles if allowed to dry out.

directions: Plant rhizome divisions in spring in wet, fertile soil in shallow standing water up to 4 inches deep or consistently saturated soil in full sun to partial shade; variegated Japanese water iris needs constant moisture and struggles if allowed to dry out. Sword-shaped leaves are crisply striped in white and green through spring and early summer, gradually fading to solid green by midsummer, providing months of bright variegated texture at a pond margin or rain garden before the deep blue-purple flowers with a yellow signal patch open above the foliage in early summer. Native to marshes and pond edges across East Asia, it tolerates standing water better than most bearded irises, making it a good structural, upright accent for the shallow-water zone of a water garden alongside pickerelweed and arrowhead. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring or immediately after flowering to maintain vigor and variegation.
sources: International Waterlily and Water Gardening Society

planting.note: Plant rhizome divisions in spring in wet soil in shallow standing water up to 6 inches deep or consistently saturated soil in full sun to partial shade; dwarf cattail spreads by rhizome and is best confined to a submerged container in a small or formal pond.

directions: Plant rhizome divisions in spring in wet soil in shallow standing water up to 6 inches deep or consistently saturated soil in full sun to partial shade; dwarf cattail spreads by rhizome and is best confined to a submerged container in a small or formal pond. Narrow, grass-like leaves rise to a modest two feet, far shorter than the towering native common cattail, topped in summer by small, plump, rounded brown flower spikes that give the same classic cattail silhouette in a scale appropriate for a small water garden or container pond. Its compact size and much less aggressive spread compared to standard cattails make it one of the few cattails suitable for a residential-scale pond without quickly overwhelming the space, though it still spreads steadily by rhizome if left unconfined in open soil. Divide congested clumps every two to three years in spring to control spread and maintain vigor.
sources: International Waterlily and Water Gardening Society

planting.note: Float rooted divisions directly on the surface of a warm, still, full-sun pond well after last frost; mosaic plant needs consistently warm water above 65°F and is grown as a warm-season annual outside frost-free zones.

directions: Float rooted divisions directly on the surface of a warm, still, full-sun pond well after last frost; mosaic plant needs consistently warm water above 65°F and is grown as a warm-season annual outside frost-free zones. Diamond-shaped, glossy, bronze-green leaves arranged in tight, overlapping, geometric rosettes float flat on the water's surface in a striking mosaic or tile-like pattern unlike any other pond plant, punctuated by small, bright yellow, five-petaled flowers that open just above the leaf rosettes on sunny days. Native to slow-moving tropical waters of South America, it spreads by runners across a still pond surface and is a favorite accent for a formal or tropical-style water garden, though it needs warm, calm water and full sun to thrive and perform well. Where winters bring freezing water temperatures, bring a few rosettes indoors to a warm, sunlit aquarium or bowl to overwinter and restart the following season.
sources: International Waterlily and Water Gardening Society

planting.note: Plant rhizome divisions in spring in rich, wet, mucky soil in shallow standing water up to 6 inches deep in full sun; Manchurian wild rice spreads by rhizome into large colonies and is best grown in a submerged container to control spread.

directions: Plant rhizome divisions in spring in rich, wet, mucky soil in shallow standing water up to 6 inches deep in full sun; Manchurian wild rice spreads by rhizome into large colonies and is best grown in a submerged container to control spread. Tall, broad, bamboo-like leaves rise from the water's edge, and in East Asia the swollen base of stems infected by a specific smut fungus is harvested as a prized vegetable known as jiaobai or gaobai, with a mild, sweet, water-chestnut-like crunch used widely in Chinese cooking. Grown mainly as an ornamental water-garden accent in Western gardens for its bold, architectural foliage, it also serves the same erosion-control and habitat role at a pond margin as other tall emergent grasses, providing cover for waterfowl and other wildlife. Confine the spreading rhizomes to a large submerged container in most garden ponds to prevent it from overtaking the entire margin.
sources: Purdue University Center for New Crops and Plants Products

planting.note: Direct sow or transplant after last frost into rich, heavy soil kept flooded with 1-2 inches of water through the growing season in full sun; Duborskian rice is a short-season, cold-adapted paddy variety that can mature even in cool-summer northern climates.

directions: Direct sow or transplant after last frost into rich, heavy soil kept flooded with 1-2 inches of water through the growing season in full sun; Duborskian rice is a short-season, cold-adapted paddy variety that can mature even in cool-summer northern climates. Bred in Russia for a much shorter and more cold-tolerant growing season than typical rice, it is one of the few rice varieties that home gardeners in temperate, non-tropical climates can realistically bring to harvest, maturing in around 100 days compared to 150 or more for most tropical rice. Grow it in a lined kiddie pool, stock tank, or purpose-built paddy bed that can hold standing water, keeping the bed flooded through most of the growing season and draining it as the grain heads mature and dry down in late summer. Hand-harvest by cutting whole seed heads once grains have hardened and the plant has yellowed, then dry, thresh, and hull before cooking.
sources: Purdue University Center for New Crops and Plants Products
